menu_gris: I want to talk to Gris.
OFFER_01: Say, matey... me coffee's still hot. Fancy a bit o' chatter with old Caspian?
OFFER_02: Har! That's enough treasure fer one tide. Sit a spell, the pot's just brewed.
OFFER_03: Ye look like ye could use a breather, gup. How 'bout a cup o' joe and a yarn?
OFFER_04: Ahh, me knees say it's time to sit. Ye'll keep an old man company, won't ye?
OFFER_06: Arright, arright. Back to yer chests, then! The coffee and me ain't goin' anywhere.
OPEN_01: Mr.Caspian takes a long sip and sighs like a ship coming into harbor.
OPEN_02: Ahh... nothin' like a fresh cup down in the deep. Don't be shy now, ask old Caspian whatever ye like.
OPEN_04: Old Caspian don't bite... much. Gyahahar! Go on, ask away.
OPEN_05: I got all the time in the seven seas. What'll it be?
OPEN_06: Back fer more o' me yarns, eh? Can't say I mind.
OPEN_07: Same cup, same old Caspian. What'll it be today, gup?
OPEN_08: Ye know, I been savin' a story or two fer ye.
OPEN_09: Ahh, there's me favorite minnow. Sit, sit.
OPEN_10: Coffee tastes better when there's someone to share the quiet with. What'll we talk about?
OPEN_11: Ye've become a regular down here, ye know that? Darlin' would like ye.
CLOSE_01: That's the bottom o' the cup. Back to yer chests, matey!
CLOSE_02: Har! Talked me throat dry. Same time next tide?
CLOSE_03: Thanks fer listenin' to an old sea dog. Off ye go, now.
CLOSE_04: Mind the current on yer way, gup. And come back soon, y'hear?
CLOSE_05: Already? Well, the coffee won't drink itself. Off ye go!
CLOSE_06: Har! Just wanted the company, eh? I'll take it.
CLOSE_menu: End of the talk, and the skip
S1_01: Mr.Caspian leans back. The chair creaks like an old mast.
S1_03: As ye know, name's Mr.Caspian. To you, at least. The "Mister" is important. I earned it.
S1_04: I been livin' a while now, but I'm only old enough fer a couple o' granguppies. Don't ye go thinkin' I'm some rottin' old geezer!
S1_05: Did ye know a tortoise can live past a hundred and fifty years? I ain't a tortoise yet. Close, though. Gyahahar!
S1_06: I own a little cafe in the place above this hut. Nothin' too special... but we might have the best coffee in town, at the least!
S1_07: Anyhoo... I like watchin' how this world shifts and changes. So many amazin' things out there, comin' and goin' like doodles in the sand.
S1_08: The tide takes the doodle, sure. But somebody saw it before it went, and that's what counts.
S1_09: Gettin' older ain't half as bad as ye think, kiddo! Ye just get more stories and fewer knees.
S1_11: Not with me chests, though. Flattery don't open locks. I've tried.
S1_o01: You don't look old at all!
S1_12: Ask anyone upstairs! Well... ask the ones that like it bitter.
S1_13: The ones that like it sweet will tell ye we've got the best SUGAR in town. Also true.
S1_14: Not much of a talker, eh? That's fine. Old Caspian talks enough fer two.
S1_15: Fer three, if ye ask the parrot.
S2_01: Oh, me? Just a bit o' gardenin' and a cup o' joe.
S2_02: He lifts the cup, as if to prove it.
S2_03: I drank grog on the sea me whole life, so this quiet livin' is just right fer old Caspian now.
S2_04: Gardenin's a lot like sailin', ye know. Ye watch the weather and mind the water. Most days nothin' happens... until everything happens at once.
S2_05: Here's one fer ye: a tomato's a fruit. A proper berry, even. Took me sixty years to learn that, and I'm still a little upset about it.
S2_06: I was quite the curious fish even back then, y'know. Always lookin' fer somethin', and not once did I know what it was!
S2_07: Even now that I've settled, I'm learnin' new things all the time. The young'uns nowadays are all over the place. Phones that take pictures! Pictures that talk!
S2_08: That's to say, I like hearin' 'bout people's lives. Everybody's so different... even old Caspian learns somethin' new every day!
S2_09: That ye can't dry a sock in a toaster. Don't ask.
S2_10: ...Some lessons ye only need once, gup.
S2_11: It is, 'til a snail eats yer lettuce in the night. Then it's war.
S2_12: Quiet war. Very slow. Snails ain't fast, but they're patient.
S4_01: Mr.Caspian laughs so hard he has to put his cup down.
S4_02: Honestly, that's quite flatterin', minnow! Those ain't no sea windows. They're aquarium tanks, built by yours truly.
S4_03: I built 'em when I first dug out this little cave, with as many reinforcements as I could fit while still keepin' it pretty.
S4_04: Here's a secret: big tanks like these ain't even glass. It's acrylic, thick as a dictionary. Glass that thick would look green and weigh more than a ship's anchor.
S4_05: The room next to this one gives easy access fer feedin', cleanin'... or, man, even jumpin' in!
S4_06: I don't jump in anymore. Last time, I came out with a crayfish hangin' off me beard. He wouldn't let go fer an hour.
S4_07: All sorts o' critters live in there, happy as can be. They each got their own jobs that keep it runnin' like a system.
S4_08: The snails clean the glass, and I clean up after everyone else. Guess who's the lowest rank on this ship?
S4_09: Gyahahar! Don't let 'em hear ye. They're the true captains down here.
S4_10: ...Aye. Every captain ends up the cabin boy of his own aquarium.
S4_menu: Behind you, are those sea windows?
S3_01: Nothin' beats our house roast. A good ol' black coffee, that's what I'd say.
S3_02: He takes a slow sip, eyes closed, like a man tasting a memory.
S3_03: Did ye know a coffee bean ain't a bean at all? It's the seed of a little red cherry. Folks been roastin' cherry pits fer centuries and callin' it breakfast.
S3_04: There's an old tale that goats found it first. Ate the cherries and danced all night! Never trust a goat with a full cup, that's what I say.
S3_05: The young'uns like all that sweet stuff. Matcha with the syrups and whatnot. Too sweet fer old Caspian, but ye're about their age, so maybe ye'd like it.
S3_06: A drink's a bit like a person, gup. Bitter on the first sip, and then ye learn what's underneath.
S3_07: Whatever ye pick, it won't be BAD. Not in my cafe!
S3_08: Har! A bitter-drinker! I knew I liked ye.
S3_09: Most folks yer age make a face like they bit a lemon. Ye've got an old soul.
S3_10: Heh. I'll tell 'em to go easy on the syrup... no promises.
S3_11: Last kid who asked fer "extra sweet" got a cup that was mostly sugar and a bit o' hope.
S3_menu: What do you recommend at your cafe?
S5_01: I love music. All them melodies, stories, emotions... all of it.
S5_02: Back in the day, I used to take me old accordion out on deck, and the whole crew'd sing shanties together.
S5_03: Shanties weren't just fer fun, mind ye. Ye sang 'em to pull the ropes together. One man calls, everyone heaves on the same beat. A good song's worth ten extra arms.
S5_04: And sound carries further in water than in air. Four times faster, they say. On calm nights we'd swear the whales were singin' back.
S5_05: I still play every now and again. Sometimes just fer meself to hear... sometimes fer the regulars upstairs, when they ask nice.
S5_06: Music tells ye things words are too shy to say. Remember that, gup.
S5_07: If ye catch me in a good mood... and with a full cup!
S5_08: The accordion wheezes worse than me, though. Two old bellows, the both of us.
S5_o01: Would you play for me someday?
S5_09: Do ye now? Then ye know what I mean. Music says what words can't.
S5_10: Next time, hum me somethin'. I'll pretend I'm not impressed.
S5_menu: What does music mean to you?
S8_01: I suppose I could introduce a couple of 'em.
S8_02: He turns in his chair and points at the glass behind him.
S8_03: Ye might see shrimps and crayfish scuttlin' 'round the bottom. They're small, so they're hard to spot.
S8_04: Fun fact, free o' charge: a shrimp's heart sits right in its head. Imagine that! Every thought ye have, yer heart's right there listenin'.
S8_05: There's a lobster down there too, and that fella's been alive forever. Had him a decade or two, at least!
S8_06: Lobsters never really stop growin', ye know. They just keep sheddin' their shells and gettin' bigger. If he outlives me, he'll be the size of a rowboat.
S8_07: Now and then ye'll see jellyfish, some normal fishes, and other little critters comin' and goin', keepin' the whole thing like an organized machine.
S8_08: The jellies got no brain and no heart, and they've been around longer than the dinosaurs. Makes ye wonder what brains are even fer.
S8_09: Most of 'em come from different places, but they all like the same kind o' water. Funny how that works, eh? Folks ain't so different.
S8_10: Admiral. He earned it. He's outlasted three heaters and a flood.
S8_11: I salute him every mornin'. He never salutes back, the rude old crustacean.
S8_o01: Does the lobster have a name?
S8_12: Not a one! And they're still doin' better than some sailors I knew.
S8_13: Ninety-five parts water out of a hundred. The rest is attitude.
S8_menu: Tell me about the sea creatures there!
S19_01: These? Bits and bobs from all over the seas. Every port had somethin' worth keepin'.
S19_02: He pats the nearest chest like an old dog.
S19_03: Most of it's just shiny trinkets. Spoons, mostly, and a teapot shaped like a goose. Don't ask about the goose.
S19_04: Some things ye pick up 'cause ye can't bear to leave 'em behind. A shell from a beach ye'll never see again... it keeps the beach fer ye.
S19_05: Old sailors used to tuck a coin under the mast fer luck when they built a ship. I've got a whole chest o' them coins. The ship didn't need 'em all.
S19_06: And some things I lock up 'cause they're too strange to sell! Gyahahar!
S19_07: That's a tale fer another tide, gup.
S19_08: Some things are better talked about when ye know each other better. Trust is like cheese. It needs time.
S19_09: Har! Only with the proper keys, ye cheeky barnacle!
S19_10: And only if the keys don't snap. They snap a lot, and I'm not sayin' I enjoy it. ...I do enjoy it.
S19_menu: Where do all these chests come from?
S28_02: Look at me, gup. I'm an old man. Me knees creak louder than me chests, and me sailin' days are long behind me.
S28_03: But a pirate never stops lovin' a good hunt. He just switches sides.
S28_04: So now I hide the keys, and the young'uns go lookin'. At my age, there's nothin' better than organizin' a treasure hunt this big! Gyahahar!
S28_05: He rubs his hands together, very pleased with himself.
S28_06: Did ye know real treasure maps hardly ever had an X on 'em? Mostly it was directions. "Forty paces from the crooked tree", that sort o' thing. Then the tree falls over, and good luck to ye.
S28_07: I hid one o' me own keys so well once, I spent a week lookin' fer it. Found it in me slipper.
S28_08: Mark me words, though: a key ye found yerself turns sweeter than one ye were handed.
S28_09: That's the idea! Keeps ye young, and keeps me entertained.
S28_o01: That's a lot of work for me!
S28_10: Course it is. The hunt's the best part of any treasure. The treasure's just the excuse.
S28_menu: Why do I have to search for the keys myself?
S6a_01: I guess so. Always super late on rainy nights, a pretty young lady comes into the cafe. Prolly in college. Curly blue hair, emerald eyes.
S6a_02: Ye know that smell when rain hits dry ground? There's a fancy word fer it: petrichor. She taught me that one. Smart lass.
S6a_03: I chat with her every now and then. Sometimes I miss a word or two, 'cause she's quiet and washin' dishes gets loud. But y'know, it is what it is.
S6a_04: Last time I saw her, she asked me somethin' kinda interestin':
S6a_05: "Theoretically, let's say you get a feeling that there's only one person, a stranger, who understands you more than anyone... but you always miss your chance to talk to them. What would you do?"
S6a_07: Of course, old Caspian just said: "Why not just say somethin'?" Even just a "Hi", y'know.
S6a_08: Most chances don't knock, gup. They walk right past ye, whistlin'. Ye gotta wave.
S6a_09: But even so, it's got me wonderin'... what on earth is goin' on in that lady's life?
S6a_10: Love, eh? Ye might be onto somethin', gup.
S6a_11: Love makes folks quiet, or loud. Never in between.
S6a_12: That's what I told her! Great minds, eh?
S7_01: One o' me old crewmates needed help repairin' the ship one day.
S7_02: Somehow, windows came up, and he rambled on 'bout how he'd experimented with tanks, windowed ships, stuff like that.
S7_03: That man sure could talk... but he was prolly a genius, all things considered! Haven't heard from him in ages. People come and go.
S7_04: He's the one who told me water's heavier than it looks. A tank this size holds more weight than a whole herd o' cows. Every wall's holdin' a little sea back.
S7_05: When I first came to this town, I was so curious 'bout how all that worked. Studied up a lot, tried all kinds o' tanks, before decidin' it'd just be nicer to make an aquarium.
S7_06: Me first tank leaked so bad, I had a fish swimmin' in me slippers by mornin'.
S7_07: Took a while to gather the loot fer the big purchases, so fer a while it was just a frame down here. Luckily the cafe got popular, so it didn't take too long.
S7_08: Anything worth buildin' gets built twice, gup: once in yer head, once with yer hands. The first one takes longer.
S7_09: Every bolt. Well... most bolts. Some bolts I built with a lot o' cursin'.
S7_11: Couldn't tell ye. Last I heard, he was buildin' a submarine out of a bathtub.
S7_menu: How did you build all this?
S9_01: Down here? Har! No, no. I live upstairs, right by the cafe.
S9_02: This place is me vault. A place just fer me... and fishes like you.
S9_03: He looks around the cabin fondly.
S9_04: Every old sailor needs a quiet hold fer his things. Upstairs is noise and cups and orders. Down here, it's just the hum o' the tanks.
S9_05: Most folks up there don't even know it exists. I'd like to keep it that way, so mum's the word, eh?
S9_06: Old pirate rule: the best treasure's the one nobody's lookin' fer.
S9_08: If ye ever spill, I'll know. The fish tell me everything.
S9_09: Just me family, and they don't care much fer it. They got their own discoveries to make.
S9_10: Family's a bit like the tide, gup. They go out, but they always come back.
S10_01: Do I! A whole crew of 'em!
S10_02: The kids are all grown now. Some of 'em have kids of their own. Me granguppies! Sweetest little minnows ye ever saw.
S10_03: Did ye know seahorse dads are the ones that carry the babies? I told me kids that when they were little. They made me carry the groceries fer a week.
S10_04: And then there's me Darlin'. Finest first mate a man could ask fer.
S10_05: For a moment, his smile goes soft.
S10_06: But that's enough 'bout me family fer one cup. Ye'll hear about 'em plenty, I'm sure!
S10_07: Enough to crew a small boat, if they'd ever agree on who rows.
S10_09: Oho, curious fish! Ask me another day, and I'll tell ye proper.
S10_10: Some stories need a fresh pot.
X_01: Mr.Caspian follows your gaze to the glass. His voice drops a little.
X_02: Oh, her? That's Gris. She's seen and been through a lot.
X_03: Found the poor gup real hurt on the road. Broken wing, messed-up knees. She could barely walk, had no home, and no proper memory of one.
X_04: She's terrified o' the ocean, so I offered her some shelter in this old place. She's taken a likin' to the tanks. Nice light, and close to all of us.
X_05: The missus has been tendin' her wounds. She's recoverin' little by little... but she's still hurt in more ways than I could count.
X_06: Ye know how a crab grows? It has to crawl out of its old shell, and fer a while it's all soft and scared o' everything. Then the new shell hardens.
X_07: I think she's in her soft time, gup. Best let her come 'round in her own time.
X_08: I know ye will. That's why I told ye.
X_09: Not yet. Wave if she looks. That's plenty fer now.
X_10: Trust is like fillin' a tank: go slow, or ye crack the glass.
S27_01: Mr.Caspian's grin fades a little. He glances at the chests behind you.
S27_02: Ah. Them. Ye've got a sharp eye, gup.
S27_03: Those scores ain't from any shop. I fished 'em out o' the sea, a few at a time, over a great many years.
S27_04: They're forbidden relics... You know music has a strong force. I think maybe somebody, long ago, had a bad incident with one of these sheets o' music, and tossed 'em in the deep.
S27_05: Too strange, too wild. That's what they said, I reckon.
S27_06: But a pirate's business is keepin' what other folks throw away! One man's junk is another man's chest o' gold.
S27_07: And who knows? Some of 'em might be relics of a distant past. Music nobody remembers writin'.
S27_08: The deep's a good keeper, ye know. Cold, still water slows everything down. Old wrecks can last centuries down there, longer than on any shore.
S27_09: So I keep 'em locked up nice and safe. If ye manage to open one... play it with respect, gup. It waited a long time fer somebody to hear it.
S27_10: Folks who thought they knew what music ought to sound like.
S27_11: Never met one who was right about that.
S27_12: I know ye will. Ye've got the hands fer it. And the stubbornness.
S27_menu: Why are there music scores in some of the chests?
S6b_01: Sure. Lately, while I was tendin' the garden, I saw an amber-colored, feline-lookin' fella.
S6b_02: He had on these foresty clothes and these chunky silver gloves. He was walkin' 'round our town like he was lookin' fer somethin'.
S6b_04: Never saw anyone like him before, to be honest. Had me wonderin' where he's from. Those gloves especially stuck out to me.
S6b_05: In me sailin' days, ye could tell a sailor's job by his hands. Rope burns fer the deckhands, ink stains fer the navigator.
S6b_06: I got a feelin' those gloves are hidin' a story like that. More than some chunky new fashion trend.
S6b_07: Or a very fancy gardener! I'll ask him 'bout his roses next time.
S6b_08: Heroes and gardeners got a lot in common. Both pull out what don't belong.
S6b_09: Nah. He looked busy. Some folks ye let walk past, and wish 'em luck.
S6b_10: I left a cookie on the fence fer him, though. It was gone by mornin'. Him or a raccoon, I'll never know.
S11_02: He sets down his cup and straightens his coat, as if she might walk in.
S11_03: I've got a wonderful wife. Call her Mrs.Marisol. Gorgeous platinum locks, diamond-like eyes, and a life-changin' smile.
S11_04: Sailors always called their ships "she", ye know. Some say it's 'cause a ship needs care, and gives it back tenfold. I say they just hadn't met Darlin' yet.
S11_05: If ye see her out 'n' about in town, tell her I sent ye. I'm sure she'd fix ye biscuits and tea, on the house.
S11_06: Now, if it was ME, ain't no way I'd let that slide. Them biscuits are too scrumptious to give away without a nickel or two.
S11_07: But that woman's as sweet as can be, I tell ye. She won't let me charge anyone fer 'em! Gyahahar!
S11_08: All these years, gup, and she still laughs at me jokes. That's the real treasure. Don't tell the chests.
S11_09: She is. Lovelier than me, which ain't hard.
S11_11: Really! The cafe loses a fortune on 'em.
S12_01: The cafe? Ye're a silly fish, askin' me that. Ye can always just stop by, it's right 'round the corner!
S12_02: Well, the whole family works up there together. We live right by it, yet we spend most of our time in there. It's fun. I quite like it.
S12_03: Mornings are fer the regulars. Same faces, same orders. Some of 'em I could serve with me eyes closed. I've tried. Spilled a lot.
S12_04: Afternoons are fer the students and the travellers. That's when the stories come in. Everybody brings a little piece o' the world with 'em.
S12_05: The kids mostly stay outta here. They're all grown, and none of 'em care to be down here much.
S12_06: With how the times change, wouldn't surprise me if they've found a world COMPLETELY different from the one I sailed through!
S12_07: That's the thing 'bout gettin' old, gup. Ye stop bein' the explorer, and start bein' the port. Folks sail out from ye. That's a fine job too.
S12_08: Then do! Order the house roast and tell 'em Caspian sent ye. They'll charge ye double, out o' spite.
S12_11: ...Me daughter. Don't tell her I said that second part.
S17_01: Darlin' likes a little cocoa and milk in hers. That's pretty great too.
S17_02: Tastes like her hugs feel. That warm house roast, with a gentle sweetness from the chocolate. Very motherly.
S17_03: Here's somethin' ye might not know: long ago, folks paid with cocoa beans. A pocketful could buy ye a meal. Imagine payin' fer yer cocoa with... cocoa.
S17_04: And I'll say this: me doodlebug daughter learned somewhere how to make a MEAN chocolate chip cookie. I dunno how she does it!
S17_05: I asked fer the recipe once. She said "a pinch o' love". I added a pinch o' love. Burnt 'em anyway.
S17_06: Only if ye get there before the granguppies do!
S17_07: They hunt them cookies like gulls around a fishin' boat.
S17_08: Sweetest crew I ever sailed with. And I sailed with a LOT o' crews.
S17_09: Most o' them smelled worse, too.
S18_01: Pirate's a strong word, gup. I prefer "sailor with flexible rules".
S18_03: Like I said, I was a curious fish. Always lookin' fer somethin', never knowin' what. The sea seemed big enough to hide whatever it was.
S18_04: Here's a pirate secret fer ye: most of us never buried a single treasure. Ye spend it, or ye lose it. Diggin' holes is a lot o' work fer a man who just wants a nap.
S18_05: And the eyepatches? Some say ye kept one eye used to the dark, fer when ye went below deck. Clever, if it's true. I just had a bad eye fer a month.
S18_06: There were a couple other little reasons I sailed, but that's it fer the most part.
S18_07: ...Aye. I think I did. Just not where I expected.
S18_08: Sometimes ye sail the whole world, and the treasure's waitin' on a pier.
S18_09: Terrifyin'! Ask the crew. They called me a big softie behind me back.
S18_10: I made 'em scrub the deck fer it. Very terrifyin'.
S18_menu: Why did you become a pirate?
S13_02: I met her back in me pirate days, when we found her hometown. Walkin' 'round that place fer the first time... it was just about love at first sight when I caught a glimpse of that woman.
S13_03: Ye know sailors steer by the North Star? It's the one star that stays put while all the others turn. When I saw her, I knew I'd found mine.
S13_04: I was so head over heels, I ain't got no reason fer anything I did that day other than to get her attention.
S13_05: I may have fallen off the pier twice. The second time on purpose.
S13_06: It's a bit of a long story, gup. I'll tell ye more 'bout it another time.
S13_menu: How did you and Mrs.Marisol meet?
S6c_01: Well, the other night, a spirit-lookin' fella stepped into the cafe and sat at the bar. Super cool lookin'. Couldn't tell if it was a lad or a lass.
S6c_02: It had these big tails like the sea's lovely waves. Had me reminiscin' 'bout the old days. Glowin' white pupils, flame-lookin' horns, a little feline-ish.
S6c_03: After sippin' a bit o' the mocha Darlin' made, it asked me: "Have you ever seen a large, warrior-like man with glowing eyes around here? He's not quite human, and has a lot of fluffy hair..."
S6c_04: We talked a while. Seemed the one it was after was its sweetheart. It turned into a whole conversation 'bout love and whatnot.
S6c_05: He goes quiet for a moment.
S6c_06: Strangest thing... I got a feelin' that little minnow had been lovin' that man fer longer than I've loved Mrs.Marisol.
S6c_07: Some love's like a lighthouse, gup. It keeps shinin', whether the ship comes back tonight or in a hundred years.
S16_01: Truth be told, I got too attached to a couple critters at sea. There was a little octopus I took in as me own, after rescuin' him from the shore.
S16_02: Did ye know an octopus has three hearts? And blue blood! That little fella was more of a noble than any captain I sailed under.
S16_03: Clever, too. He learned to unscrew jars to get at the shrimp. One day he unscrewed the jar, climbed out o' the bucket, and ate me sandwich.
S16_04: When it was time to settle on land, I was... a little troubled 'bout lettin' the fella go back to the sea.
S16_05: So much so that Darlin' insisted I absolutely could NOT just let him go on his own. She said I sounded like a broken record every time I brought it up!
S16_06: Her and that lovely smile convinced me to make a nice big space fer him to stay.
S16_07: He lived in buckets and little tanks fer quite a while, but when I finally finished it, he was one happy pup, that's fer sure.
S16_08: He's been gone a while now, but I think he lived a happy life. And now all these other cool folk get to live here too. Ain't that somethin'!
S16_09: Captain Inkbeard. The crew named him. I ain't proud of it.
S16_10: He liked it, though. He'd turn red every time we said it. Octopuses change color when they feel things, ye know. He felt a lot.
S16_o02: He was lucky to have you.
S16_menu: Is there a reason you built the aquarium?
S14_01: Ye want the WHOOOLE story, kid? Well, I'll be!
S14_02: He refills his cup to the brim. This will take a while.
S14_03: Arright, from the very top, then.
S14_04: I met her back in me pirate days, a little past halfway through that whole era, so to speak. On the shore of a pretty far town. Not a different country or anything.
S14_05: Lemme tell ye, that lady was such a beaut, the whole crew just about called me crazy!
S14_06: I convinced 'em to hang 'round that town a while, just so good ol' Caspian could shoot his shot, y'know what I'm sayin'!?
S14_07: I bought her flowers from every stall in town. She said she was allergic. ...She wasn't. She was just teasin' me. I married a pirate, gup.
S14_08: One thing led to another, and we got her on our crew. They made fun of me fer actin' so tough while bein' such a lovebird, but I could NOT help it, kiddo. She was just too sweet.
S14_09: She learned the ropes faster than half the crew. Could tie a bowline with her eyes shut. I still can't, and I've had all me life to learn.
S14_10: Soon enough, I learned she liked me too. Yer Mr.Caspian was overjoyed, that's fer sure.
S14_11: That's about it, kiddo. Is it what ye were hopin' to hear?
S14_12: Har! Don't tell the crew I told ye. I got a reputation.
S26_02: He looks at the tanks for a long moment.
S26_03: But the sea ain't goin' anywhere. I hear it in the tanks every single day.
S26_04: Ever wonder why the sea's salty and rivers ain't? Rivers carry a pinch o' salt from every rock they pass, and the sea keeps all of it. Never gives a grain back.
S26_05: Sailors are the same. We keep a pinch of every place we've been.
S26_06: And everything I went lookin' fer out there... turned out it fit in a little cafe. Funny, ain't it?
S26_07: Bah! Ye're gettin' as sappy as me.
S26_08: Only if Darlin' comes. And she gets seasick now. So, no.
S29_01: Ahh, me gate! Ye like it? Designed it meself.
S29_02: Locks are older than ye'd think, by the way. Some o' the first ones were wooden bolts with little pins that dropped into place, thousands o' years ago. Folks have been keepin' secrets fer a long, long time.
S29_03: Greed, Pride, Envy and Wrath. Four keys, and every one of 'em is a fight a treasure hunter has to win before he's worth his salt.
S29_04: I built it so only the strongest ever get a chance at me treasures. Most folks give up at the first lock.
S29_05: He looks at you over the rim of his cup.
S29_06: Ye ain't the first student I've seen walk through that gate, ye know. There've been a few others, over the years.
S29_07: And when ye first came in, I saw the same thing in yer eyes I saw in theirs. That stubborn little spark. Determination, they call it.
S29_08: Ye'd be surprised how rare it is to keep it lit.
S29_09: But I'll tell ye the real reason, since ye've been so good to an old man.
S29_10: This place is me own little corner o' the world. I keep a few souvenirs down here... the very few I never had the courage to show Mrs.Marisol.
S29_11: Don't look at me like that! Nothin' bad. Just old sailor's things. A man's allowed a secret or two.
S29_12: The kind that stay in the vault, gup.
S29_13: ...Fine. One of 'em is a very bad love poem I wrote fer her and never gave. Gyahahar!
S29_14: Good kids, every one. Some of 'em still send me postcards.
S29_15: Treasure hunters have a way o' findin' each other. Maybe ye'll meet 'em someday.
S29_menu: Why does the entrance gate require those 4 keys?
S30_01: Mr.Caspian nearly chokes on his coffee.
S30_02: Gyahahar! Show HER? Me secret hideout?
S30_03: He turns the cup slowly in his hands, and doesn't say anything for a while.
S30_04: She'd prolly just laugh, ye know. Then she'd ask why I never told her.
S30_05: All these years married, and I'm still scared o' showin' her a few old souvenirs. What does that say about me?
S30_06: That I'm a coward, prolly. A coward with very good coffee.
S30_07: Secrets are like barnacles, gup. Leave 'em long enough, and they slow the whole ship down.
S30_08: Arright, arright. I'll think about it. Someday.
S30_09: And... thank ye fer worryin' about me. Not many folks worry about the old man in the basement.
S30_10: ...Aye. I think so too. That's what scares me.
S30_11: Good gup. Now don't go tellin' her I said "someday". She'll hold me to it.
S30_o02: Your secret is safe with me.
S30_menu: You should show this place to Mrs.Marisol someday.
S15_01: Well, that's a good question, kiddo.
S15_02: Eventually we had a guppy in the oven, so to speak. To make sure the delivery'd be safe, we ended our sea life and settled down in this little town. It was a lot smaller, way back when.
S15_03: First thing we bought here was a coffee grinder. Second thing was a bed. Tells ye where me priorities were.
S15_04: Inspired by some towns from the voyage, I started learnin' how to do all this cookin' and coffee stuff. Darlin' taught me plenty too... partly to impress her, bein' honest.
S15_05: Ye know a fathom's the stretch of a man's arms, fingertip to fingertip? Our first cafe was about three fathoms wide. "Cozy," Darlin' called it. "Cramped," I called it.
S15_06: While she took care of our first little gup, I opened the cafe.
S15_07: Everything else came with the flow o' life, y'know. Kids grew up, kids had kids. I'm happy bein' a grandpa. Those little minnows are just the sweetest.
S15_menu: When did you two end up in this town?
S25_02: The little ones think this hut is a pirate ship. They ain't wrong... but I don't let 'em down here. Too many chests to trip on.
S25_03: Last week the littlest one asked me if fish sleep. They do, ye know. Eyes open, 'cause most fish got no eyelids. Just driftin' and dreamin'.
S25_04: She tried sleepin' with her eyes open after that. Lasted four seconds.
S25_05: They sneak cookies off the counter when they think Darlin' ain't lookin'. She's always lookin'. She just lets 'em.
S25_06: Grandkids are the best part of gettin' old, gup. All the fun, none o' the night shifts.
S25_07: Takes after their granddad, that lot. Gyahahar!
R1_01: Dark as the deep and twice as strong. Just how I like it.
R1_02: He takes a long sip and sighs happily.
R1_03: They say a light roast has a touch more kick than a dark one, scoop fer scoop. Everybody thinks dark is stronger. It's just louder.
R1_05: Me first captain drank his coffee so strong, ye could stand a spoon up in it. One mornin' he did. The spoon stayed there till lunch.
R1_06: He lived to ninety-one, that man. Never slept past dawn a single day, but he lived to ninety-one.
R1_07: Moral o' the story: everything in moderation. Except stories. Ye can never have too many stories.
R1_08: Burnt it a little. Don't tell anyone upstairs.
R1_09: I was readin' the paper and forgot the pot. Smelled it from three rooms away.
R1_10: Rule o' the galley: never turn yer back on a pot or a parrot.
R1_11: Ye know why burnt coffee tastes so bitter? Roastin' turns the sugar in the bean sweet and brown, same as toast. Too long, and it all turns to char.
R1_12: Still drinkable, though. Burnt coffee's like a sea story. Bitter, but ye finish it anyway.
R1_13: And then ye tell everyone it was wonderful. Gyahahar!
R1_14: New beans from a little farm up in the hills. A bit fruity. I'm still decidin' if I like it.
R1_15: He holds the cup under his nose and breathes in, slow and serious.
R1_16: Coffee likes the mountains, ye know. The higher it grows, the slower it ripens, and the more flavor it packs in.
R1_17: Same with people. The slow ones are the interestin' ones.
R1_18: The farmer sent a letter with the sack. Says his goats keep tryin' to eat the cherries. Some things ain't changed since the old tale, eh?
R1_19: I wrote back: "Keep the goats. Send more beans." Good business is mostly short letters.
R1_20: Just right. Coffee's the one thing in life ye shouldn't rush.
R1_21: Boilin' water scorches the grounds, did ye know? Ye let it rest a breath after the kettle sings. Just a breath.
R1_22: Same with tempers. Let 'em rest a breath before ye pour 'em out.
R1_23: ...That one was wise. Write it down.
R1_24: He waits, as if you might actually write it down.
R1_26: Gyahahar! It's fine. I'll say it again next week. Old men repeat the good ones.
R6_01: Turn the key gentle, like ye're wakin' a sleepin' kraken.
R6_02: Or don't! I enjoy the snappin'. Gyahahar!
R6_03: ...I'm jokin'. Mostly. A key's like a promise. Force it, and it breaks.
R6_04: Me old bosun used to say: if it don't turn, don't push. Wiggle. Life's mostly wigglin', gup.
R6_05: He also said never eat soup on a Tuesday. Not all his advice was good.
R6_06: The fancier the chest, the fancier the key. That's the law o' the sea.
R6_07: Old locks had little walls inside, wards, they're called. Only the right key's shape slips past 'em.
R6_08: A key keeps a secret with one lock, and one lock only. Very loyal things, keys.
R6_09: Very romantic, locks. Don't tell the chests I said that.
R6_10: And don't go tryin' a plain key on a golden chest. The chest'll be insulted. I'll be insulted. Everybody'll be insulted.
R6_11: Don't ye go punchin' me chests if a key snaps. I've seen that look in yer eye.
R6_12: Them chests have crossed more oceans than you've had breakfasts. Storms, and one very angry walrus.
R6_13: Punch a chest, and the chest remembers. I've seen one hold a grudge fer twenty years.
R6_14: It wouldn't open fer the fella that kicked it. Not with any key. Opened fer me first try.
R6_15: Coincidence? I think not. Be nice to the furniture, gup.
R6_16: Every chest runs dry eventually, gup. Even treasure's got a bottom.
R6_17: When one's empty, don't be sad. An empty chest just means somebody got lucky.
R6_18: Usually you. Sometimes the parrot. Don't ask how.
R6_19: And an empty chest's still a good chest. Ye can put new things in it. Socks, or a sandwich fer later.
R6_20: Not fish, though. I learned that the hard way. Took a week to air out.
R10_01: Ah, that's an old record from upstairs. Smooth, ain't it? Goes good with coffee.
R10_02: Records are just grooves, ye know. A tiny needle rides a tiny canyon, and out comes a whole band.
R10_03: Like magic, if magic came in a paper sleeve.
R10_04: I found this one at a market in a port town, years back. The seller swore it was cursed. Said it made people fall in love.
R10_05: Bought it on the spot. Worked, too. Not on me, on the seller. He married the fishmonger the very next month. Gyahahar!
R10_06: Jazz, gup! Shanties are fer the deck. This is fer the deep.
R10_07: The trick with jazz is the players listen to each other more than they play. Half the music's in the listenin'.
R10_08: Same with a good talk. Which is why I'm doin' all the talkin'. Wait. Hmm.
R10_09: He frowns at his cup, deep in thought.
R10_10: Arright, arright. Next time, you talk and I listen. ...Right after this story.
R10_11: The record skips at the same spot every time.
R10_12: As if on cue, the music hiccups.
R10_13: There! Hear it? I've grown to like the skip. Feels like the song's catchin' its breath.
R10_14: Everything old's got a little skip in it, gup. Me knee skips on the stairs. Me memory skips on Tuesdays.
R10_15: Don't go fixin' every skip ye find. Some of 'em are where the character lives.
R10_16: Darlin' and I danced to this one once. Badly. Very badly.
R10_17: I stepped on her feet eleven times. She counted. She still brings it up on anniversaries.
R10_18: She says a good dance ain't about the steps. It's about who ye step on.
R10_19: I think she meant it sweet. I'm still not sure.
R4_01: Once, we chased a giant squid fer three days. Whole crew sharpenin' harpoons, the cook prayin' in the galley.
R4_02: He spreads his arms as wide as they go.
R4_03: Turned out it was a lost hat. A very big hat, with a feather.
R4_04: The feather alone was longer than our cook. And our cook was a tall man.
R4_05: The captain wore it fer the rest o' the trip. Called it his "trophy". Gyahahar!
R4_06: Real giant squids exist, mind ye. Eyes as big as dinner plates. Never met one, and never wanted to.
R4_07: There was a fog so thick, the cook served soup into it by mistake.
R4_08: Ye couldn't see yer own boots. We rang the ship's bell every minute so nobody'd bump into us.
R4_09: Ships blow horns in fog too, long and low, so others know where ye are. Sounds like a cow with a broken heart.
R4_10: Our horn was broken, so the cook mooed. Fer six hours.
R4_11: We never found the soup. Some nights I still wonder where it went.
R4_12: That's what fog teaches ye, gup: when ye can't see, listen.
R4_13: One night the whole sea glowed blue around the ship. Not a sound, just light.
R4_14: Every wave, every oar stroke, sparkled like we were rowin' through stars.
R4_15: Tiny critters, too small to see, that glow when the water moves. Billions of 'em.
R4_16: I dipped me hand in, and it came out sparklin' fer a second. Like I'd caught a handful o' night sky.
R4_17: I still dream about it. Some things ye see once, and they keep ye company forever.
R4_18: A storm once threw a fish straight into me boot. Flipped right in like it paid rent.
R4_19: I named him Boots and put him right back in the water. Good fella.
R4_20: Sailors say whistlin' on deck calls up the wind. And never bring bananas aboard. Bad luck, both of 'em.
R4_21: I whistled once, in that very storm. The crew still hasn't forgiven me.
R4_22: I never believed the banana one, either. Then a banana fell on me head that same night. Make o' that what ye will.
R4_23: We found an island that wasn't on any map. One palm tree, and a crab that looked very surprised to see us.
R4_24: We camped there a night. Next mornin', it was gone. Just sea.
R4_25: Prolly a sandbar, and the tide came in. Prolly.
R4_26: I still keep a bit o' that sand in a jar, in one o' them chests. Nobody believes me. That's fine.
R4_27: The sea lends ye a place fer a night, then takes it back. Ye keep the memory. She keeps the sand. Mostly.
R5_01: The tomatoes are fightin' the snails, and the snails are winnin'.
R5_02: Did ye know a snail's got thousands o' teeth? Tiny ones, on a tongue like a file. That's how they get through me lettuce so fast.
R5_03: I've tried everything. Eggshells, then stern words. Mostly stern words.
R5_04: He shakes his fist at an imaginary snail.
R5_05: Me neighbor says I should share with 'em. I say the snails should share. They never offer me anything.
R5_06: Planted some mint fer the cafe's iced drinks. It's takin' over everything.
R5_07: Mint sends out runners under the dirt, sneaky as a smuggler. Plant one, and next year ye've got a hundred.
R5_08: Mint's a pirate, I tell ye. A true pirate. I respect it.
R5_09: They say mint keeps mice away, too. Me cellar's full o' mint and I've still got a mouse.
R5_11: Grew a pumpkin so big, the granguppies tried to sail it.
R5_12: Pumpkins are fruit too, did ye know? Everything good in me garden turns out to be a fruit. I feel lied to.
R5_13: The biggest pumpkins in the world weigh more than a small car. Mine weighed about as much as a big dog. A respectable dog, mind ye.
R5_14: We carved a face in it. Looked just like me. Darlin' says it's the handsomer one.
R5_15: I'm choosin' not to take that personally.
R3_01: The lobster molted again. Left his old shell lyin' 'round like dirty laundry.
R3_02: After a molt, he hides fer days 'til the new shell hardens. A soft lobster's a nervous lobster.
R3_03: Did ye know lobsters taste with their legs? Little hairs on their feet. Imagine tastin' the floor with every step.
R3_04: Explains why he walks so slow. He's savorin' it.
R3_05: I bring him extra snacks when he's soft. He pretends not to care. He cares.
R3_06: Two crayfish had a fight over the same rock. There's three rocks. Nobody wins.
R3_07: He mimes two tiny claws snapping at each other.
R3_08: Crayfish can grow back a lost claw, ye know. So they fight like they got spares.
R3_09: Don't fight like a crayfish, gup. Ye only get the one set o' fingers.
R3_10: The third rock just sits there, ignored. I relate to that rock.
R3_11: A couple new jellyfish drifted in from the feedin' room. They're settlin' in nice.
R3_12: Ye know what ye call a bunch o' jellyfish? A smack. A smack o' jellyfish!
R3_13: Best word in the whole sea. I say it to customers fer no reason.
R3_14: Jellies just drift wherever the water takes 'em. No plan, no map. And they've been doin' fine fer half a billion years.
R3_16: The fish crowd 'round whenever Gris swims. I think they like her.
R3_17: Fish feel the water move with a line along their sides. She swims so gentle, I reckon they feel safe.
R3_18: He glances at the tank, a little proud.
R3_19: Maybe they know somethin' 'bout her that we don't.
R8_01: Upstairs, insultin' the customers. They tip more when he does. I don't understand it.
R8_02: Parrots can learn hundreds o' words. Mine learned eleven, and nine of 'em are rude.
R8_03: The other two are "coffee" and "Caspian". I choose to believe that's love.
R8_04: Last week he called a customer a barnacle. The fella laughed so hard he ordered a second slice o' cake.
R8_05: He hates the damp down here. Says so, too. Loudly.
R8_06: Smart birds, parrots. Some solve puzzles better than kids. Mine figured out how to open the cookie tin... and how to close it again, so nobody'd know.
R8_07: The missus caught him red-handed. Well, red-feathered. He looked her dead in the eye and said "coffee".
R8_08: She gave him a cookie anyway. I've never been so proud of a criminal.
R8_09: Old fella's older than some o' me chests. Still sharp as a hook.
R8_10: The big parrots can live sixty, seventy years. He'll prolly outlive me, and then insult whoever buys the cafe.
R8_11: That's what I call a legacy!
R8_12: Somewhere far upstairs, very faintly, something squawks. It sounds a lot like "barnacle".
R2_01: Rainy day, so business is good. Everybody wants somethin' warm.
R2_02: Folks shake off their umbrellas at the door like wet dogs. The floor's a lake by noon.
R2_03: I put a sign up: "No swimmin'". Nobody laughed. The sign's still there.
R2_04: Old sailors could smell a storm a day off, ye know. The air gets heavy, the gulls fly low. I still get a twinge in me knee. Better than any forecast.
R2_05: The grinder broke again. I fixed it with a spoon and pure stubbornness.
R2_06: The first grinders were just two stones, did ye know? Folks crushed the beans by hand. I almost miss it. Stones don't break.
R2_07: Machines are like ships, gup. They creak and complain, and they keep goin' if ye talk to 'em nice.
R2_08: I talked to it very nice. Then I hit it with the spoon.
R2_09: A bunch o' students came in after class, loud as gulls. Reminded me of ye, gup.
R2_10: They ordered six drinks and one cookie, and split the cookie six ways. Very fair. Very sad.
R2_11: Sharin' a cookie six ways is the most sailor thing I ever saw. On a ship, ye share everything. Even the bad soup.
R2_12: I gave 'em five more cookies. Don't tell the till.
R2_13: Darlin' baked biscuits this mornin'. I'd bring ye some, but... well. They didn't survive the stairs.
R2_14: There's thirty-one steps from the kitchen to this hatch. I counted. One biscuit per step. ...The biscuits ran out at step eight.
R2_15: There are crumbs in his beard.
R2_16: I'm on a diet, apparently. Darlin' says so. The biscuits disagree.
R7_01: Not much, gup. A seagull stole a whole croissant off a table upstairs. Bold bird.
R7_02: Gulls are smart, ye know. They watch what ye eat, and they wait. Patient as a harbor master.
R7_03: The customer cried. The gull looked very proud. I gave the customer a new croissant and the gull a stern look.
R7_04: The gull did not care about me stern look.
R7_05: A kid tried to pay fer cocoa with a seashell. Darlin' took it!
R7_06: Said it was a fine shell, and fair's fair. Now it sits by the till. We call it the bank.
R7_07: Every mornin' I check the bank. Still one shell. Very stable economy.
R7_08: That blue-haired lady ain't come by in a while. Hope she finally said hi to someone. Hope they said hi back.
R7_09: Rain's been light lately, too. Maybe she only comes with the rain. Some folks are like that.
R7_10: I set a cup aside fer her anyway, every rainy night. Just in case.
R7_11: Saw that feline fella with the silver gloves again, at the edge o' town. Still lookin' fer somethin'.
R7_12: He nodded at me. I nodded back. Then I raised me cup, like a toast.
R7_13: He seemed to understand. Good man.
R7_14: Whatever he's lookin' fer, I hope he finds it. Or it finds him. That's usually how it goes.
R9_01: Same as always. Swims, stares at the fish, naps. She said the lobster winked at her.
R9_02: Lobsters ain't got eyelids, so I don't know what she saw. I told her he winks at everyone. Now she winks back.
R9_03: Rough day. Her shape went all wobbly again this mornin'.
R9_04: The missus sat with her 'til it settled, hummin' her an old lullaby. Seemed to help.
R9_05: Some hurts ye can bandage. Some, ye just sit with.
R9_06: She's been watchin' the jellyfish fer hours. Says they move like they're not scared of anything.
R9_07: I told her that's 'cause they got no brain. She thought about it fer a long while, then said "... How familiar...".
R9_08: She's been starin' at the old phone in the back like it's gonna bite her.
R9_09: Jumps every time it rings. Then looks sad when it's fer me.
R9_10: Ye could ring her, ye know. Just sayin'. An old man can hint.
R9_11: She's been quiet since yer call. Wouldn't tell me what it was about. Said it was hers to tell.
R9_12: Fair enough. Every old sailor's got a story or two he keeps locked in his own sea chest.
R9_13: Ring her again sometime. Some things take more than one try to say.
R9_14: She's been hummin' some tune lately! Ain't never heard her hum before.
R9_15: Asked her where it came from. She just smiled. Well, as close as she gets to smilin'.
R9_16: She hums it to the fish, and they seem to like it. The lobster's unconvinced.
R9_17: She stands by the side window every even day, ye know. Every second day, like clockwork. If ye want to say hi proper, that's when.
R9_18: She asks 'bout ye every day. "Is {player} coming today, Sir Caspian?" Every. Day.
R9_19: On odd days she sulks in the tank. On even days she's at the window an hour early.
R9_20: She made somethin' fer the lobster too. He seemed unimpressed. Lobsters are like that.
R9_21: She says she's makin' somethin' fer me next. I hope it's a cookie. It's prolly a scarf.
R9_22: She's been standin' a little taller since she told ye. Ye noticed?
R9_23: She told the lobster too. He took it well, fer a lobster.
R9_24: Trust takes years to grow and a second to drop, gup. Mind it well.
E1_01: Mr.Caspian sets his cup down and fishes something out of his coat.
E1_02: Say, gup... ye've been good company down here. Better than most.
E1_03: Here. That's the number fer the cafe phone. Ring me up when ye're not down here, if ye fancy a chat.
E1_04: He hands you a coffee coaster with a number scribbled on the back: 75EA5.
E1_05: Read it slow: seven, 5, E, A, 5. Make pretend 'ose fives are the letter S, and it's... The seven seas! Took me a whole week to get the phone company to give me that one.
E1_06: The phone's older than me parrot, so ye may have to shout a bit. And if the parrot answers, hang up. Just hang up.
E1_07: Don't go givin' it to the granguppies, either. They'd call me every five minutes.
E1_09: Bah. Thank me with good company.
E2_01: Mr.Caspian glances at Gris, then back at you. He lowers his voice.
E2_02: Listen, gup. Remember what we talked about on the phone?
E2_03: I think Gris needs a friend. A real one. Not just an old sea dog like me.
E2_04: He slides a folded sheet of paper across the counter. It is covered in numbers, all crossed out in careful, shaky handwriting, except one. It is circled: 0.?.>.#.
E2_05: She wrote that herself. Took her a whole week to work up the nerve. Said she wanted ye to have it.
E2_06: She folded it into a little boat first. I had to unfold it. Don't tell her.
E2_07: Give her a ring sometime. She won't bite. ...Probably.
E2_08: Gris told me some stranger rang her up outta nowhere. Scared her half to death... then she couldn't stop talkin' about it.
E2_09: That was you, weren't it? Gyahahar! I knew it.
E2_10: He slides the same folded sheet across the counter anyway, with her number circled.
E2_11: Well, now ye got it proper. From me. Means I trust ye with her. Don't make me regret it.
E2_12: Gris told me some stranger rang her up a while back. Wouldn't say what they talked about. Only that it was... hers.
E2_13: I had a hunch it was you, gup. Gyahahar! Don't worry, I ain't askin'.
E2_14: Whatever it was, she's been lighter since. Hums to the fish, even.
E2_15: He slides the folded sheet across the counter, with her number circled.
E2_16: Now ye've got it from me, fair and square. She stands by the side window on even days. Next time she's there, come say hi.
CALL_01: Best coffee in town, how can I help ye? ...Oh, it's you, gup! Hold on, lemme step away from the grinder.
CALL_02: Ahoy! Ye caught me between two orders. Make it quick... or don't, the customers can wait!
CALL_03: Hello? Speak up, gup, the lunch crowd's loud as a storm today!
CALL_04: Fair winds, gup! Come see me down below soon.
CALL_06: The line is busy. Mr.Caspian must be serving customers. Try again tomorrow.
CALL_07: Har! The lunch crowd's pourin' in, gup. That's all the chatter I got fer today. Ring me tomorrow!
CALL_08: Oop, the grinder's callin' me. Duty before stories, gup. Same time tomorrow?
CALL_09: Darlin's givin' me the look from the counter. Back to work fer old Caspian. Call me tomorrow, aye?
CALL_menu: Picking up, hanging up, busy, and back to work after the topic
CALLEARLY_01: Best coffee in town, how can I help ye?
CALLEARLY_02: Deliver? Har! Only down the stairs, and nobody lives down there. Come by the cafe, matey!
CALLEARLY_03: No harm done! If ye're ever thirsty, the cafe's right 'round the corner.
CALLEARLY_06: Best coffee in town, how can I help ye?
CALLEARLY_07: ...Hold on. I know that voice. Ain't you the gup who keeps turnin' keys down in me vault?
CALLEARLY_08: How'd ye get this number? Never mind. A good sailor never asks where the wind found its secrets.
CALLEARLY_09: Can't chat now, the lunch crowd's a storm up here. Come see me down below, and we'll have a proper cup.

CP1_01: Busy! A whole school trip came in. I've made forty cocoas.
CP1_02: Me arm's gonna fall off. If it does, I'll stir with the other one.
CP1_03: Cocoa froths better if ye whisk it in a figure eight, ye know. Darlin' taught me that.
CP1_04: A child's voice in the background asks for "the pirate cocoa".
CP1_05: That's me cue. The "pirate cocoa" is just cocoa with a little paper flag in it. Sells twice as well.
CP1_06: Quiet. Just me, the parrot, and a fella who's been readin' the same newspaper since mornin'.
CP1_07: I think he's asleep. I've been refillin' his cup anyway. Feels rude not to.
CP1_08: Quiet days are good days, gup. Ye notice the small things. The way the steam curls. The way the parrot pretends he ain't watchin' the cookie tin.
CP1_09: Rainy, so we're packed. Darlin's runnin' the counter like a captain on deck.
CP1_10: I've been demoted to dishes. Best seat in the house, though. I can hear every story from the sink.
CP1_11: Somebody lost a cat, somebody found the cat. Busy town.
CP1_12: The grinder's makin' a noise like a seal with a cold. I'm talkin' to ye from under the counter.
CP1_14: There. Fixed. Spoon again. Spoon fixes everything.
CP1_15: If ye ever need somethin' fixed, gup, ye know who to call. Bring yer own spoon.
CP2_03: She says hello, that ye're too skinny, and that there's biscuits waitin' fer ye whenever ye come up.
CP2_04: She also says I talk too much on the phone. She's right. Don't tell her.
CP2_05: She's out walkin' with Gris. Doctor's orders: fresh air.
CP2_06: Gris holds her hand the whole way. Darlin' pretends it's to help her walk. It ain't.
CP2_07: They stop at every flower. Every single one. It's a very slow walk. Best kind.
CP2_08: She's knittin' somethin' by the window. Won't tell me what. Says it's a surprise.
CP2_09: Last surprise she knitted was a sweater fer the parrot. He wore it once and bit a customer.
CP2_10: The customer still comes in every week. Asks if the parrot's wearin' the sweater. Funny how folks get attached.
CP2_11: She's teachin' the granguppies to bake. The kitchen looks like a snowstorm hit it.
CP2_12: Flour on the ceiling, gup. The CEILING. I don't know how. I'm afraid to ask.
CP2_13: But the cookies came out right, and the little ones are proud as admirals. Ceilings can be washed.
CP3_02: The noise of the cafe fades, as if he stepped into another room.
CP3_03: I'm sure that makes the two of us, wondering... what exactly that girl might be.
CP3_04: We got no clue what kinda place she's from. But she's got roots in somethin' far, far deeper down.
CP3_05: Tell me, kid. Ever met someone whose clothes turn monochrome the moment they put 'em on?
CP3_06: That ain't exactly normal. I've seen some strange things and strange folk, but they look normal next to her.
CP3_07: And the poor girl's always in some kind o' pain. Her shape keeps shiftin'. Sometimes she takes the form of other people, normally just fer a moment.
CP3_08: I worry 'bout her often. But there ain't much I can do but let her swim in the tank. That's her favorite.
CP3_09: I knew givin' ye this number was a good call. Most of the folks who know 'bout her ain't sharp enough to catch that I didn't just take her in fer shelter and care.
CP3_10: Her energy, her vibe, her nature... it kinda reminds me o' some of the artifacts I've collected. Don'tcha think?
CP3_11: Not today, gup. Call me another day.
CP3_12: Maybe. Or maybe she needs more than an old man and a fish tank.
CP4_01: Arright. Ye remember them chests that were too strange to sell?
CP4_02: A compass that points at whatever ye miss most. A coin that's never the same color twice. And a few I ain't even got names fer.
CP4_03: Things that ain't quite from here. Things that feel like they're waitin' fer somethin'.
CP4_04: Old sailors used to say the sea keeps what it can't understand. Maybe that's why I keep 'em. Somebody has to.
CP4_05: Gris feels like that. Like she's waitin'... and she don't even know fer what.
CP4_06: I ain't sayin' she's a trinket, mind ye! She's a girl, and a sweet one. I'm sayin' she might be part o' somethin' bigger than this little town.
CP4_07: Keep an eye on her fer me, will ye? When the time's right.
CP5_01: Different? Aye, now that ye mention it.
CP5_02: She's been hummin'. Gris! Hummin'! Some tune I never heard in all me years at sea. Darlin' nearly dropped a tray.
CP5_03: I asked her where she picked it up. She looked at me real quiet, and said it was hers.
CP5_04: Old crews had songs like that. Verses made up on one ship and sung on no other. Ye didn't ask what they meant. Ye just let 'em sing.
CP5_05: Whatever happened, it did her good. If ye had a hand in it... thanks. I won't pry.
CP6_01: Before ye say anythin', gup... she told me. Came all the way up the stairs to say it, on those sore legs. First time she's done that.
CP6_02: Ye understand what that means? That girl's been scared o' near everything since the day I found her on that road.
CP6_03: Trust ain't a thing ye hand back. Ye just carry it, careful, like a full cup on a rollin' deck.
CP6_04: ...Gyahahar! Listen to me, gettin' misty over the phone. Darlin' says hello. And that ye're still too skinny.
CP6_05: Now then. What did ye call about?

GP2_03: She scared the crayfish half to death the first time. Now they follow her 'round!

GP2_09: Maybe... if someone I trust is there... maybe...

GP2_o03: Can I watch you swim sometime?

GP3_08: A silly cat statue, made from clay. Its face looks just a little bit familiar.
GP3_09: I um... On a walk the other day, there was a gray cat with a dark bandana that looked at me with these big "silly" eyes.
GP3_10: I never saw anything like it before, and Sir Caspian called it "silly" when I explained it to him later... So I tried to make a cat that looked like it... I hope it's the kind of thing you like...
GP3_11: An assortment of flowers in a glass vase. It's a very bright collection, and looks picked by hand.
